messages:
owen: quick check — I'm proposing a small rollout tweak for the model-api statefulset to reduce tail latency spikes during scale events. plan is: split replicas across two zones with unequal weights (3 + 1), switch updateStrategy to RollingUpdate with partitioning, and set maxUnavailable: 1, maxSurge: 0. want to avoid full-az blast when we do image rollouts. snippet below — does this look sane?

owen: ```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: model-api
spec:
  replicas: 4
  updateStrategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      partition: 1
  template:
    spec:
      topologySpreadConstraints:
      - maxSkew: 1
        topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
        whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
        labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: model-api
``` 

owen: terraform will also change the azAffinity map to pin 3 replicas to zone-a and 1 to zone-b via nodeSelector patch. I added a canary for 10% traffic for the new image for 15m. question: any concerns around PVC attachment ordering or pv detach flakiness with this partition approach? @sasha @lina

sasha: sounds reasonable. PVC ordering might be okay since we keep partition=1 (so one pod stays on old version). main risk is if zone-b has different disk perf — we should add a readiness gate that checks disk io before traffic. also make sure the storageClass has volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer.

lina: +1 to readiness gate. also, if the nodeSelector changes, we should run a terraform plan and then a terragrunt apply in staging first. can you paste the terraform diff? would like to confirm no implicit replacement of PVs.

owen: pasted plan in the staging channel — TL;DR terraform wants to update the node_selector on the statefulset template (in k8s_manifest module) and will create a new replicaSet for the daemon that manages sidecar. no PV replacements in plan. infra-bot: can you run the storageClass/SC check for us?

infra-bot: storageClass check: 1) model-ssd sc has volumeBindingMode=WaitForFirstConsumer 2) CSI driver version matches cluster operator 3) no pending PVs in staging. :white_check_mark:

devon: quick note on rollout: with partition=1, the controller will not touch the first partitioned ordinal (ordinal 0) — to fully complete upgrade you need to set partition=0 at the end. plan for manual step: after canary window and perf checks, set partition: 0 to finish. also watch for headless svc DNS propagation for stateful pods — some apps query peers by ordinal.

sasha: +1. add a Prometheus alert for pod start latency and PVC attach errors during the canary window. I can add a temporary rule and remove after rollout.

lina: I'll review the tf plan now. @owen add a short runbook in the PR description: steps, rollback commands (kubectl rollout undo / terraform apply with previous map), and who to ping. maybe include quick k9s commands to check ordinal bindings.

owen: thanks — will update PR. one more tiny ask: our KMS key rotation happened last week — does the secret provider sync handle re-mounts if we change nodeSelectors? wanted to avoid leaking old creds.

infra-bot: secret-controller note: when nodeSelector/pod move occurs, secret-provider-csi will refresh at pod start; it will attempt to remove old mount and re-mount new volume. recommended: restart the pod after kubelet mounts to ensure latest secret version. no known leakage observed in staging.

devon: good. I'll be on standby for the final partition=0 flip. owen — drop the PR link here when ready and I'll approve. :thumbsup:

owen: PR up: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/+/9876 — includes manifest, terraform patch, and the short runbook. thanks everyone.

sasha: reviewing now, will add alert rule.

lina: looks clean from TF side — approving staging apply.

devon: approved for rollout after canary metrics look stable.
